# Camera

[Toolkit](README.md) · `DotGame.Toolkit.Graphics` · class

```csharp
public sealed class Camera
```

A view of a 2D world: where it looks, how close, and at what angle. Begin a sprite batch with its [`Transform`](#transform) to draw the world through it.

## Example

```csharp
camera.Position = player.Position;
using var batch = spriteBatch.Begin(camera.Transform);
```

## Properties

### Origin

```csharp
public Vector2 Origin { get; set; }
```

Gets or sets where on the screen [`Position`](#position) appears: the top-left corner by default, and the middle of the view for a camera that follows something.

### Position

```csharp
public Vector2 Position { get; set; }
```

Gets or sets the point in the world the camera looks at.

### Rotation

```csharp
public Angle Rotation { get; set; }
```

Types: [`Angle`](https://github.com/hotchaipro/DotGame.Framework/blob/main/docs/api/Framework/Angle.md)

Gets or sets the camera's angle. The world appears to turn the other way.

### Transform

```csharp
public Matrix3x2 Transform { get; }
```

Gets the transform from the world to the screen, for `SpriteBatch.Begin`. To use it with a [`ViewportScaler`](ViewportScaler.md), multiply it by the scaler's: `camera.Transform * scaler.Transform`.

### Zoom

```csharp
public float Zoom { get; set; }
```

Gets or sets how close the camera is: above 1 magnifies the world, and below 1 shows more of it.

**Throws `ArgumentOutOfRangeException`:** The value isn't positive.

## Methods

### ScreenToWorld

```csharp
public Vector2 ScreenToWorld(Vector2 screen)
```

Gets the point in the world at a point on the screen, such as a pointer's position.

### WorldToScreen

```csharp
public Vector2 WorldToScreen(Vector2 world)
```

Gets where a point in the world appears on the screen.
